newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary relaxes grip on state companies.
newsitem.headline: Hungary relaxes grip on state companies.

text.p: The Hungarian parliament on Tuesday cleared the way for the private sector to increase its stake in certain companies by reducing the state's compulsory holding.

The legislature amended the privatisation law to allow the state-owned stake in the national telecom company Matav and the commercial bank OTP to be reduced to one special rights "golden" share from 25 percent plus one share.
OTP, owned by a large number of domestic and international investors and the state, is Hungary's largest commercial bank.

Matav, which is 67 percent owned by a 50-50 consortium of Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech Corp, holds a monopoly on national and international long-distance terrestrial telephone communications in Hungary.

The parliament also cut the compulsory state stake from 50 percent plus one share in drugs wholesale company Hungaropharma Rt to one special rights share and to 25 percent plus one share in the national broadcaster Antenna Hungaria Magyar Musorszoro es Radiohirkozlesi Rt.

The parliament decided that the government should hold a golden share in meat processor Pick Szeged Rt and in electrical equipment factory Ganz Ansaldo Rt, majority-owned by the Italian Finmeccanica group.
Other changes affect about fifty companies.
The special shares will ensure veto right for the state in decisions on capital hikes and reductions mergers and other questions.

The amendment of the privatisation law was approved by 200 votes in favour, 57 against and 9 abstentions, with the government coalition parties supporting the law and the opposition parties voting against it.

Opposition speakers said the aim of the amendment was to boost 1997 privatisation revenues, but the changes were ill-prepared, while the government did not clarify its budgetary targets with the new sales and did not ensure sufficient rights for the state in the companies.
Analysts said earlier that the reduction of the compulsory state stake in Matav and OTP to one golden share would stimulate the markets but still leave room for government intervention.
